decisions.reason: As a newly launched, close-to-core handle in a growing market, it still has option value and likely low carrying costs, though its standard character makes it somewhat easier to prune than more distinctive launches.
A new door lever handle family fits the firm's broad established range and can serve multiple projects, so management would usually keep it while market acceptance is still unfolding.
This new handle design is near the firm's core design-led offer, and with little evidence yet that demand has failed, the firm would keep the option open.
Because it is another close-to-core design variant in a firm that competes on breadth and design quality, it is more likely to be retained than withdrawn after only a short market test.
A handle family strengthens system breadth across customer needs and budget levels, so in the absence of clear negative signals the firm would likely continue offering it.

The electronic access system matches the firm's strategic move toward digital building organization and was launched as a distinctive innovation, giving strong reasons to retain it despite higher development intensity.
